Layer 1 FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY LOTTERY REGULATORY OFFICE (FCT-LRO)
The Federal Capital Territory Lottery Regulatory Oﬃce (FCT-LRO) hereby informs gaming
operators, industry stakeholders and the general public that the Oﬃce has commenced
operations as the regulatory authority responsible for the oversight, regulation and supervision
of gaming activities within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
Following the Supreme Court judgment in Attorney-General of Lagos State & 21 Others v.
Attorney-General of the Federation & 15 Others, Suit No. SC/1/2008, the constitutional
position on the regulation of lotteries and gaming has been clarified. By virtue of Section
299 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended),
the FCT has a distinct constitutional status, with the National Assembly exercising
legislative powers ordinarily vested in a State House of Assembly.
Accordingly, gaming operators conducting business within the FCT are required to comply
with the applicable FCT licensing and regulatory requirements and engage with the FCT-
The Oﬃce clarifies that the Supreme Court judgment did not expressly settle the full
regulatory framework applicable to online gaming. In particular, the judgment did not
establish that any one State has exclusive regulatory control over the online gaming
Accordingly, the online gaming market remains open to operators and investors. Operators
are free to choose the regulator from whom they wish to obtain their gaming licence or
authorisation, based on their business model, operational needs and the regulatory
framework they consider most suitable and beneficial to their business.
This choice may be exercised without undue interference, intimidation or coercive
treatment by any State regulator solely on the basis that an operator has elected to obtain its
licence from another regulator, as every state is duly empowered to regulate gaming
Operators are, however, reminded that the online nature of a gaming platform does not, in
itself, exempt an operation from applicable licensing and regulatory obligations where
The FCT-LRO remains committed to providing a transparent, consistent and predictable
regulatory environment for digital gaming operations within the Federal Capital Territory.
All gaming operators previously licensed by the National Lottery Regulatory Commission
(NLRC) who are currently operating, or intend to operate, within the Federal Capital
Territory (FCT) are hereby required to approach the FCT-LRO to regularise their regulatory
The Oﬃce further clarifies that any NLRC licence that remains valid and has not expired
will be recognised for the remainder of its validity period and converted to the
corresponding FCT-LRO licence. Accordingly, holders of former NLRC licences will
retain the benefit of their unexpired licence terms, subject to the regularisation process
Aﬀected operators are required to present and hand over their former NLRC-issued
licences for verification and documentation, complete the applicable regularisation
